words.definition: to put an end to something
words.example: Many states have abolished the use of cell phones while driving.

words.definition: being in complete disorder and confusion
words.example: The traffic in Seoul is often chaotic.
The governor made a controversial decision to raise truces.
The recent downturn in the housing industry exemplifies the poor economic conditions.

words.definition: to account for something while making a decision or analysis
words.example: The family had to factor in the price of gasoline as they planned their road trip.
words.zh: 在做決定或分析時考慮某些事情

words.example: In 2008, the United States economy began to falter dramatically.

words.definition: giving pleasure or a feeling of accomplishment; showing thanks
words.example: It was gratifying to see the injured bird recover and return to the wild.
words.zh: 給予快樂或成就感；表示感謝

words.example: The company launched a new program to attract more clients.
The engineer had a legitimate reason for changing the design of the building.

words.definition: a lack of energy or commitment; lazy; indifferent
words.example: The hippopotamus basking in the sun displayed almost total lethargy.
words.zh: 缺乏精力或承諾；懶惰的;冷漠

words.example: The speaker has a particular way of persuading his audience.

words.definition: sending out in all directions, especially heat or light
words.example: The actor's radiant smile captivated the audience.
words.zh: 向各個方向散發，尤其是熱或光

words.definition: the length of time or distance from one limit to the other; to cross
words.example: The old man's life spanned two centurtes.
words.zh: 從一個極限到另一個極限的時間長度或距離；穿越

words.example: The spontaneous combustion inside the cylinder creates the power of the motor.

words.definition: a natural flow of something; a pouring out
words.example: There was a constant stream of information coming from the White House.
words.zh: 事物的自然流動；傾瀉而出

words.example: His striking proposal saved the company from bankruptcy.
